children: The latest Commitments of Traders report from the CFTC, released September 25, shows large speculators holding a net long position of 2,756 Bitcoin futures contracts on the CME as of September 22. That's an increase of 288 contracts from the prior week, a modest but steady climb in bullish positioning.
Total open interest in Bitcoin futures jumped by 1,542 contracts to reach 22,315.

Large speculators, the category the CFTC labels "non-commercial traders," are the hedge funds, commodity trading advisors, and other institutional players who trade futures for profit rather than to hedge an underlying business exposure.

On the other side of the trade sit the commercials. These are typically entities hedging real exposure, and they're net short 3,109 contracts. That short position actually shrank by 452 contracts from the previous week.

Each CME Bitcoin futures contract represents 5 BTC. So the speculative net long of 2,756 contracts translates to roughly 13,780 BTC worth of bullish exposure. The commercial net short of 3,109 contracts equates to about 15,545 BTC in hedged downside protection.
Then there's the leveraged funds category, which as of the September 15 data was net short 6,354 contracts.

The same report shows that traders increased both long and short positions in S&P 500 futures. In currency markets, speculators maintained net short positions in the Swiss franc, British pound, and euro.

The COT report has become an increasingly useful tool for reading institutional sentiment in crypto. When Bitcoin futures launched on the CME in December 2017, they were a novelty. Now they're a fixture of institutional portfolio construction.

The persistent commercial net short of more than 3,100 contracts suggests that entities with direct exposure to Bitcoin's price are actively hedging against a pullback. The reduction of 452 contracts from the previous week indicates they are covering some bearish bets but not exiting their positions.

The previous week's leveraged fund net short of 6,354 contracts represents a substantial pocket of capital that could either fuel a short squeeze if prices rally further, or prove prescient if the market rolls over.
The next COT report is scheduled for October 2.

title: CFTC reports Bitcoin net long position of 2,756 contracts for week of September 22nd
